_instructions: DEPRECATED for routing. This file is install + display metadata only — what's installable, its name/emoji/tagline, min_budget, risk_level, install command derivation, and (for variant families) the base_skill + selector mechanism. For ALL strategy-recommendation routing — which skill to recommend when a user says X, the conversational flow to walk a user through, how to handle variants, how to disambiguate between similar strategies, default selections, ordering for display in a recommendation UX — the canonical source is the Decision Tree at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Senpi-ai/senpi-skills/main/senpi-trading-runtime/references/producer-patterns.md (Layers 0-3, plus the 'Live fleet roster — archetype mapping' table at the bottom). When this file and the Decision Tree disagree, the Decision Tree wins. USAGE: list installable skills + their display metadata. Group by each skill's 'group' field (the archetype slug — e.g. 'single-asset-alpha-hunter', 'contrarian-unwind', 'trader-follower') and humanize for display (e.g. 'Single-Asset Alpha Hunters'). For variant families like the Thesis Funds, deploy via the base_skill listed on the variant row and pass the variant's selector value as the environment variable specified in the Decision Tree's variant section (e.g. Thesis Funds: base_skill=thesis-fund-strategy, env var THESIS=<thesis>). DO NOT INVENT quality tiers like 'Proven Performers' / 'Top Picks' / 'Best-in-Class' — there is no curated quality ranking here; differentiation is by category and thesis only. Infrastructure skills (DSL, fee optimizer, scanners) are never displayed. min_budget is the realistic platform floor (~$100 minimum to trade on Hyperliquid) and a SUGGESTED comfortable starting size — NOT a hard gate. Position size scales with budget via margin_pct; any balance at or above the floor works. Never refuse to deploy a willing user over min_budget; offer to start small or watch first instead.
